newsitem.title: USA: Belden & Blake holders approve TPG merger.
newsitem.headline: Belden & Blake holders approve TPG merger.

text.p: Belden & Blake Corp shareholders approved a merger with an affiliate of Texas Pacific Group at a special meeting on Thursday.

Belden & Blake said in a statement on Thursday that Texas Pacific will pay $27 a share for all of Belden & Blake's common stock, plus an additional amount to redeem options held by directors and executives.
A dollar value of the deal was not immediately available, but the company had approximately 11 million shares outstanding as of the end of the company's first quarter.
Of the shares voted, 99 percent, constituting 84 percent of the outstanding shares, were voted in favor of the merger.
The merger is expected to be completed on or about June 30, 1997.
Within two weeks after that date, instructions will be mailed to shareholders as to the procedures to be followed to receive payment.

"We are gratified by the opportunity to reward our long-term shareholders for their commitment and support over the past five years," said Ronald E. Huff, newly named President and Chief Financial Officer. "The overwhelmingly favorable vote by our shareholders validates our decision to merge the company," Mr. Huff continued.

Ronald L. Clements, the company's new Chief Executive Officer, said, "We are extremely enthusiastic about our future opportunities and growth potential. Our primary strategy is to aggressively pursue drilling and acquisition projects in our area of operations."

Belden & Blake Corporation is actively engaged in producing oil and natural gas, acquiring oil and gas properties, exploratory and development drilling and gas gathering and marketing in the Appalachian, Michigan and Illinois Basins.

Texas Pacific Group, based in San Francisco and Fort Worth, Texas, is the sponsor of TPG Partners II, L.P., of Fort Worth, a private investment partnership with capital in excess of $2 billion. The partnership specializes in corporate acquisitions in a wide range of industries.
